## 1. Purpose

This procedure describes how to install Eosense eosAC soil gas flux
chambers, connect them to the eosMX-P multiplexer, and operate the
Picarro G2508 cavity ring-down spectroscopy (CRDS) analyzer for
measuring greenhouse gas fluxes (N~2~O, CH~4~, CO~2~, NH~3~, and
H~2~O) from soil. The SOP also covers data acquisition using the
eosAnalyze-AC software and data export for analysis [@picarro_g2508;
@eosense_eosac].

This SOP was originally developed for greenhouse gas emission
measurements from strawberry fields in Northern California and has been
modified as new projects have come on line.


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Field deployment of the Picarro G2508 CRDS analyzer
  coupled with Eosense eosAC dynamic soil flux chambers and the eosMX-P
  multiplexer for automated soil greenhouse gas flux measurements
- **Does not apply to:** Laboratory (bench-top) Picarro configuration
  (see [SOP-F504](../lab_sops/SOP-F504-picarro-lab.qmd)), atmospheric
  concentration monitoring without flux chambers, or eddy covariance
  measurements
- **Location:** All EA Program field sites within 30 m cable reach of a
  power source

## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Compressed gas cylinders (calibration standards) pose
  crush and high-pressure hazards. The generator (if used) presents
  fuel spill, carbon monoxide, and noise hazards.
- **Chemical:** Drierite desiccant is a mild irritant. Calibration gas
  cylinders may contain pressurized gases.
- **Electrical:** Power strip, generator, and instrument connections in
  outdoor conditions; keep connections dry and off the ground.
- **Environmental:** High ambient temperatures (above 35 C) can cause
  instrument overheating.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Closed-toed shoes or field boots
- [ ] Safety glasses (when handling gas cylinders)
- [ ] Work gloves (when handling cylinders and generator)
- [ ] Sun protection (hat, sunscreen)
- [ ] Hearing protection (if generator is running nearby)

### Required Training

- [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd)
- [SOP-F101 Electrical Power in the Field](SOP-F101-electrical-power-in-the-field.qmd)

### Emergency Procedures

In case of gas leak from calibration cylinders, move upwind and ventilate
the area. For generator fuel spills, contain with absorbent materials.
Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) for general
field emergency response.

## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Sampling Design

1. Locate the Picarro analyzer, multiplexer, and pump at the base
   station. Choose a level, shaded location if possible.
2. Use a random number generator to determine the chamber placement
   locations within the study area
3. All chambers must be within 30 m of the multiplexer (the length of
   the cables and tubing)
4. If a generator is used, place it at least 100 feet downwind of the
   chambers to avoid contaminating flux measurements with exhaust

### 6.2 Hardware Setup

1. Connect the recirculation pump to the analyzer VACUUM port using the
   corrugated metal hose. Use new Swagelok washers each time.
   Hand-tighten, then seal with a wrench.
2. Connect the multiplexer to the Picarro through USB ports on the
   Picarro (any port)
3. Connect the monitor, mouse, and keyboard to the Picarro via the
   remaining USB ports (two additional ports are available on the front
   of the Picarro)
4. Connect the blue monitor cable to the Picarro and the monitor power
   cable to the outlet
5. Ensure all machines are in the off position (circle symbol = off)
   before connecting power
6. Connect power cables for the CRDS analyzer, multiplexer, and pump
7. Connect the pump to the multiplexer:
   a. Connect the control and data ports on the back of the pump to the
      Picarro, ensuring the white triangles face upward
   b. Insert the other ends into any USB port on the Picarro
8. Connect clear tubing from the pump inlet (left side, clear tube) to
   the multiplexer inlet (right side, labeled)
9. Connect the outlet tubing: multiplexer outlet to the Picarro inlet
   (clear tube); pump outlet (right side, silver tube) to the Picarro
   outlet
10. Attach one end of the power/data cable to the COMM port on the pump
    and the other end to the matching COMM port on the multiplexer

::: {.callout-important}
Never turn off the pump while the Picarro is running. Never disconnect
the vacuum while the analyzer is operating. Doing so can damage the
instrument.
:::

### 6.3 Installing Chamber Rings

Chamber ring installation varies based on experimental design.
Install rings in advance of the measurement day to minimize soil
disturbance during data collection. *TBD -- add project-specific ring
installation protocols as needed.*

### 6.4 Picarro Startup

1. Ensure all instruments are off and turn on the power strip
2. Turn on the recirculation pump first (no wait time required)
3. Switch on the Picarro. The boot-up sequence initializes the CRDS
   software and analyzer.
4. Switch on the multiplexer. The system requires approximately 30
   minutes to warm up; warning alarms are normal until the cavity and
   other components reach operating temperature.
5. Keep ambient temperature below 35 C. If the DAS temperature
   approaches 45 C, shut down or use a fan to cool the air around the
   Picarro.

### 6.5 Placing Chambers

1. While the Picarro is warming up, connect all tubing and cables.
   Route tubing along the bed surface; do not let tubes fall into
   furrows.
2. Place chambers onto the ring bases, pressing down to achieve a good
   seal. Try to avoid disturbing the chamber after installation.
3. After all chambers have opened, perform a second check for foliage
   or debris that might obstruct the chamber seal.

### 6.6 Data Collection

Once the Picarro alarm indicator is green, the system is ready.

1. Verify typical atmospheric concentrations on the Picarro display:

| Gas    | Expected Ambient Concentration |
|:-------|:-------------------------------|
| N~2~O  | Approximately 0.3 ppm          |
| CH~4~  | Approximately 2.4 ppm          |
| CO~2~  | 300--600 ppm                   |
| NH~3~  | Variable                       |
| H~2~O  | 1--5%                          |

2. Open the FP-Monitor multiplexer software
3. Uncheck "Default Cycle"
4. Load the appropriate cycle from the user folder. Available cycles
   include:

   - *TBD -- list current cycle names (e.g., "Straw 5 Chamber,"
     "Full 12," "Full 12 minus #4")*

5. When the Picarro G2508 is warm, press "Start Cycle"
6. Check all chambers to ensure good seals
7. If a generator is in use, check fuel every two hours and top off.
   Release pressure before inserting the nozzle into the filler throat.
   Open the valve and press the green button for 3--5 second intervals,
   checking between fills to see if fuel is at or near the red line.
8. Aim for at least 3 complete measurement cycles. For irrigation
   studies, target 2 cycles before irrigation, 2 during, and 2 after.

### 6.7 Shutdown

1. After at least two post-irrigation cycles (or at the end of the
   measurement period), begin retrieving chambers after each one
   completes its measurement, starting with chamber #1
2. Cap all tube ends with a glove secured by tape
3. Carefully coil each set of tubes and cables to limit twisting and
   scratching of the Teflon. Zip-tie or Velcro together and stack in
   order on the ground.
4. Remove chambers from the sampling locations. Separate bases from
   chambers and repackage into boxes.
5. When the final chamber measurement is complete, end the sampling
   cycle in the software
6. Connect a spare chamber to a channel and select the "Desiccate"
   method. Run dry air through the Picarro for 10 minutes to prevent
   condensation damage [@picarro_g2508].
7. Initiate the Picarro shutdown sequence; select the option for moving
   the instrument
8. After the Picarro has fully shut down, manually switch off in this
   order:
   a. Multiplexer
   b. Picarro
   c. Vacuum pump
   d. Power strip


## 7. Calibration

The Picarro G2508 analyzer calibration is intended to be performed
infrequently [@picarro_g2508]. The procedure requires three calibration
standards per gas species (two points define the calibration line and a
third intermediate point is used for verification).

### 7.1 Calibration Procedure

1. Select calibration standards that span the representative range of
   concentrations the analyzer will typically measure. A concentration
   of zero is acceptable for the low-end standard.
2. Introduce the first calibration standard into the analyzer for long
   enough to yield a stable reading
3. Record the stated concentration of the standard and the analyzer's
   displayed value
4. Repeat for the remaining two standards
5. Plot the data with the analyzer's reported concentration on the
   horizontal axis and the standards' stated concentrations on the
   vertical axis
6. Calculate a linear best-fit equation. The slope and intercept are
   used to apply a correction to the analyzer's factory calibration.

::: {.callout-note}

## 8. Data Export and Analysis

### 8.1 Using eosAnalyze-AC

1. On the Picarro desktop, open the "eosAnalyze-AC" program. If it is
   not on the desktop, navigate to Start Menu and search
   "eosAnalyze-AC." Open the "eosAnalyze-AC-v3.4.2" folder and run the
   `.exe` application.
2. You do not need to wait for the Picarro system to warm up if you are
   only downloading data.
3. Click "Collect Data." Enter the start and end times for the period
   you want to download. Repeat for each cycle separately; combining
   multiple non-contiguous periods into one export will produce a
   single table with large time gaps.
4. Ensure the time zone is set correctly. Pacific Time Zone is UTC-8:00.
5. Verify the data under "Measurements." Check that the correct dates,
   times, and data graphs look reasonable.
6. Click "Export Data Table" and save the CSV to the desktop or an
   accessible location.
7. To export additional data tables, close and reopen the program before
   creating each new export.
8. Transfer the `.csv` files to a USB drive or external hard drive for
   analysis on another computer. The files are compatible with Excel or
   R [@rcoreteam2024].

### 8.2 Troubleshooting Data Export

If data does not load or you see a "No measurements detected" message:

1. Go to **Data > Analyzer Data Path** in eosAnalyze-AC. The data path
   should be `\UserData\DataLog_Forerunner\`. You should see subfolders
   organized by year.
2. Click OK, then retry collecting data.
3. If the problem persists, use Windows Explorer to search for `.DAT`
   files in `\UserData\DataLog_Forerunner\YEAR\MONTH\DATE\`. The file
   naming convention is:
   `JFAADS2048-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-DataLog_Forerunner.dat`
   where JFAADS2048 is the instrument serial number, followed by the
   date and time the file was created in 24-hour format.

### 8.3 Flux Calculation

Soil gas fluxes are calculated from the rate of change of gas
concentration within the chamber headspace over the closure period. The
eosAnalyze-AC software fits both linear and exponential models to the
concentration time series for each closure event [@livingston1995;
@hutchinson1981].

$$
F = \frac{V}{A} \cdot \frac{dC}{dt} \cdot \frac{P}{RT}
$$

where:

- $F$ = flux (mass per area per time)
- $V$ = chamber headspace volume (L)
- $A$ = chamber area (m^2^)
- $dC/dt$ = rate of concentration change (ppm/s)
- $P$ = atmospheric pressure (atm)
- $R$ = ideal gas constant
- $T$ = temperature (K)

*TBD -- clarify in eosAnalyze-AC output what (L) and (E) designations
mean for flux values (likely Linear and Exponential fits). Confirm
whether "dead band range" and "chamber offset" in the data processor
options need to be set for each deployment.*


## 9. Quality Control

- Verify atmospheric background concentrations before starting each
  measurement cycle (see table in Section 6.6)
- Inspect all tubing connections for leaks before each deployment
- Check chamber seals visually and by monitoring initial concentration
  traces
- Log any chambers that fail to open or close properly and remove them
  from the dataset
- Do not disconnect chambers from the multiplexer during an active
  measurement cycle, as this can cause the data processor to miss
  measurements
- Ensure the FRMonitor software recognizes all connected chambers at
  startup; use the "System Info" button to verify. Chambers not
  recognized will not record data even if they open and close.
- Use FRMonitor software version 1.6.2 or later to schedule
  measurements

### Biases and Interferences

- Ambient temperature extremes can prevent the analyzer from
  stabilizing properly
- High-moisture gas samples can cause condensation damage. Always run
  dry air through the instrument for several minutes before shutdown
  [@picarro_g2508].
- *TBD -- develop QC criteria for acceptable flux curve fits (r^2^
  thresholds, maximum allowable dead band)*


## 10. Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                | Disposal Method                          |
|:--------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Spent Drierite desiccant  | Regenerate by heating at 210 C or dispose as non-hazardous solid waste |
| Generator fuel spills     | Absorb with spill kit materials; dispose per EH&S |
| Damaged Teflon tubing     | Standard trash (non-hazardous)           |


## 11. Training Record

Before deploying this instrument independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP, [SOP-F01 Field Safety](SOP-F01-field-safety.qmd),
   and *SOP-F04 Electrical Power in the Field*
2. Observe a trained operator perform a full deployment (setup through
   shutdown)
3. Demonstrate competence with hardware connections (pump, multiplexer,
   tubing, chambers)
4. Perform a supervised deployment including startup, data collection,
   and shutdown
5. Demonstrate ability to export data using eosAnalyze-AC
6. Be signed off by the PI or field lead


## Appendix A: Troubleshooting {.appendix}

### Days with Unexpected Data

If data appears on unexpected Julian days, check whether the system
clock or local time on the analyzer has been changed. Compare the
processed measurements against field notes to identify obvious gaps that
may correspond to mislabeled days.

### Days That Should Have More Data

Errors in FRMonitor log files can cause the data processor to overlook
measurements. If measurements appear to be missing, check the FRMonitor
logs for errors. Do not disconnect chambers from the multiplexer while
it is actively running a measurement cycle, as this can cause the data
processor to miss measurements, especially if the chamber was closed
when removed.

### Days Where Some Chambers Are Missing

If certain chambers (e.g., #1 or #2) are not sending data, this
indicates either a communication issue between the multiplexer and
analyzer or that the chambers were not connected. Verify that the
FRMonitor software recognizes all connected chambers at startup using
the "System Info" button. Disconnecting and reconnecting chambers during
a measurement cycle can also cause communication errors.

### N~2~O Noise

N~2~O measurements from the Picarro G2508 can be noisy at ambient
concentrations. *TBD -- document strategies for reducing N~2~O noise
(e.g., longer closure times, post-processing smoothing, data filtering
thresholds). Contact Picarro technical support for recommendations.*
